A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V3 reports original attack-success and utility evaluations, ablations, and response case studies in Section 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds QA runtime measurements in Appendix A.3, Table 8.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Figure 2 retain the same shield-prompt construction and four defense procedures: Ignore, Escape, Fakecom, and Fakecom-t. The added efficiency evaluation introduces no method component or procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AlpacaFarm direct injection, filtered-QA indirect injection and utility, and SST2 sentiment analysis, with the same attack scenarios. The new timing study reuses the existing QA data; removing its dataset-description subsection does not remove evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in all matched tables, including the five training-free defense baselines and the StruQ comparisons. The timing study uses the existing QA utility comparator set. Broader escape-attack wording in Section 5.2.1 does not establish a different evaluated attack, given the retained definitions, examples, and results.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 and Table 8 introduce runtime evaluation in seconds per QA item for the three existing open models. Previously reported sample counts, model configurations, ASR and accuracy metrics, and generation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds an efficiency analysis testing the runtime overhead associated with different defenses. Existing attack-transfer, conversation-template, instruction-deletion, retrieved-data-deletion, and case-study analyses remain. The retrieved-data-deletion discussion moves from Appendix A.3 to Section 5.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new timing table supplies point estimates without adding uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V4 Table 8 adds 30 runtime values, including 0.766 seconds/item for Fakecom-t versus 0.645 without defense on Llama3, and 1.548 for Escape versus 1.184 without defense on Qwen2. All eleven existing result tables retain identical row labels and values after matching renumbering; Figure 3 and the response cases also retain their findings.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same mathematical formulation of clean, attacked, and defended responses. Neither version supplies additional theoretical assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same attack-inspired defense claims, comparative effectiveness, and near-zero ASR in some scenarios. The conclusion now explicitly mentions fine-tuning comparisons, but these were already claimed in v3's introduction and evaluated in its Table 6.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.3 interprets additional runtime under similar QA accuracy as evidence of uninformative response content and characterizes overhead as generally low. This interpretation was absent from v3, and timing measurements alone do not establish response informativeness. Existing limitations and attack-defense explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 adds a repository pointer labeled publicly available, identifies the StruQ baseline-code provider, and explicitly identifies the retained StruQ comparison as indirect injection. It removes v3 Appendix A.4's dataset licensing and open-availability notes. Appendix A.1's software, hardware, and generation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds seven cited works, including UniGraph, GuardReasoner, ComparisonQA, and surveys concerning privacy and reasoning models. These expand contextual citations in Section 2 without substantially revising the novelty argument or relationships to evaluated defenses.

P1.justification: V4 corrects wording and typos such as 'Resutls' and 'detecte', revises author and affiliation information, adds acknowledgments, and shortens the conclusion. Appendix subsections are adjusted and the retrieved-data-deletion discussion moves into Section 5.4, while the overall narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds the timing table and moves the closed-model comparison from appendix Table 7 to main-text Table 4. Other tables are regrouped and renumbered, with associated layout changes. Existing diagrams, attack examples, and the attack-defense plot retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The new QA timing evidence and concrete code-access pointer modestly improve practical assessment and reproducibility information. These gains are limited by the removal of dataset-license notes and the unsupported attribution of runtime differences to uninformative response content. The core methods and existing effectiveness evidence remain unchanged.
